transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! How are you feeling after your cataract surgery? Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi there! Thanks for asking. I'm feeling pretty good overall, but I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start with light gardening, such as brisk walking, gardening, light jogging, and gentle cycling, about 1 week after surgery. However, it's best to avoid strenuous or heavy exercise, lifting heavy objects, or activities that might get water in your eyes, especially in the first month. Does that help? Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, that helps a lot, thank you! I do have another question. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should start using the preservative-free eye drops for dry eyes as soon as you can, ideally four times daily. If you've already got some, you can start using them now. If you're running out, you can get more from your GP. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Great, I'll start using the gel then. I do have another question. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: Some sensitivity to bright light is normal, especially in the first few weeks after surgery. However, if it's severe or accompanied by redness and pain, we'd want to check it out. If it's just mild, wearing sunglasses when you're outside should help. Does that make sense? Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: Some sensitivity to bright light is normal, especially in the first few weeks after surgery.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome. Do you have any other questions about your recovery or surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I have one more question. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure it's okay. Does that make sense?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, that makes sense. Thank you for the information. I don't have any more questions at the moment.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: All right, let me just check one more thing. Have all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thank you for your help!
